title: feat(plugin-gantt): refresh in place on a real query change; the initial load keeps the placeholder (objectui#7237)
body:
Fixes #7237
Clause-②: yes — published component behaviour changes: a real query change no longer tears the chart down to a placeholder.

This is the A′ half of ruling C+A′ (comment 5749198903, maintainer 「同意」). The C half landed as objectui#10407. This is the last half, hence line 1 above. Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 2 PM (claim 5828052135), session `session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`. The dispatch ran as `mode:subagent`, so that id is also this run's.

## What changes

`ObjectGantt`'s fetch effect ran every reload non-silently. Once the chart had painted, a real change to the query (sort, filter or permissions) flipped `loading`. The `if (loading)` early return then swapped `GanttView` for the "Loading Gantt chart..." placeholder, and the chart lost its scroll position, collapsed groups and in-flight edits.

- **`reload` takes two independent options.** `inPlace` keeps the chart mounted and sets `refreshing`. `silent` logs a failure and keeps the last good rows, and implies `inPlace`. Every existing `silent: true` caller behaves as before: the toolbar refresh, the four write-readbacks and the invalidation-bus reload.
- **The first load is separated from later ones.** `loadedOnceRef` flips once, when a reload first commits rows. The fetch effect runs the initial load exactly as before, with the placeholder. Every later run is in place but not silent: a changed query that fails is still reported as an error, as on base. It does not leave the previous query's rows on screen with nothing marking them stale.
- **A visible refreshing state on the chart.** The chart pane draws the shared `RefreshIndicator` from `@object-ui/components` while `refreshing` is set. It is the same indeterminate bar that `ObjectGrid`, `ListView` and `ObjectChart` draw over their rows, so there is no second convention. The pane gains `relative` to anchor the bar. Every absolute element inside `GanttView` and `ResourceWorkload` already has a positioned ancestor of its own.
- **A localized accessible name.** New key `gantt.aria.refreshing`, in `GANTT_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` and in all ten locale packs. Each value is copied from that pack's existing `list.refreshing`, so no new translation was authored. The component's default English label would repeat the objectui#3546 class: an English accessible name in every language.
- **The dependency lists are unchanged.** `reload`'s list and the fetch effect's list are byte-identical to base.
- **The objectui#7231 guard test is regenerated.** It produced its overlap from a post-paint filter change and asserted the placeholder over it, which is exactly the teardown this ruling removes. Its pairs are regenerated from the ones that still put each flag in play. Every guard assertion is kept, and a post-paint `refreshing` twin is added. The file header records why. Leg 2 and Leg 3 below show each case still fails when the guard is removed or narrowed to its own mode.

Files (15, +502/−48): `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`, `packages/plugin-gantt/src/useGanttTranslation.ts`, new `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.refreshInPlace-7237.test.tsx`, `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.staleReloadFinally-7231.test.tsx`, `packages/i18n/src/locales/{ar,de,en,es,fr,ja,ko,pt,ru,zh}.ts` (one line each), and `.changeset/7237-gantt-refresh-in-place.md` (`@object-ui/plugin-gantt` minor, `@object-ui/i18n` patch).

## Dispatch hypotheses, measured

- **H1 holds.** Measured on `origin/main` `efbf18de5`, which is after objectui#10494. The file already had `refreshing`, `reload({ silent })`, the sequence guard and the silent invalidation reload. The fetch effect called `reloadRef.current()` non-silently. Measured on the base: a sort, filter or permissions change unmounts `GanttView` (the pins below).
- **H2: the existing affordance was not visible enough to reuse on its own.** `refreshing` only disabled the toolbar refresh button and set `aria-busy` on it. That is a dimmed icon with no animation, and it is absent entirely when there is no `onRefresh` (the inline `value` provider). So this reuses the repo's existing `RefreshIndicator` and the existing `refreshing` flag. No visible string is added, only the accessible name.
- **H2 route changed.** The dispatch suggested a literal `reload({ silent: true })`. The re-query is in place but not silent, because silent would keep the previous query's rows on a failure with nothing marking them stale. Pinned: Leg 4 below reds exactly that pin.
- **H3.** The pins cover (a) to (d) as asked, and (a) and (b) are red on the base. The "2 → 1 identities" reading is not used.
- **H4.** `ObjectGantt`'s record fetch still lists `schema.filter` and `schema.sort` by identity. `ListView`'s filter hold shields it today. Neither dependency list was widened or narrowed.

## Pins, red on the base, green on the head

`ObjectGantt.refreshInPlace-7237.test.tsx`. `GanttView` is a stand-in with a once-per-mount instance id, and every `find` is held open by hand. Cases:
- Sort, filter and permissions (through a real `PermissionProvider`), each asserting:
  - (a) the same `GanttView` instance while the query is in flight and after it returns;
  - (b) the refreshing state visible while it is in flight, gone after;
  - (c) the rows replaced by the answer.
- The re-query carries the changed `$orderby`.
- (d) Control: the initial load shows the placeholder and no refreshing state.
- A failed re-query is reported, not hidden behind the previous rows.
- The zh pack labels the bar `刷新中…`.

- **Base** (pin commit `68e742a16`, base source): `Tests 4 failed | 3 passed (7)`. Readings:
  - `(a) GanttView was unmounted by the re-query …: expected 'unmounted' to be '1'`
  - `(b) no visible refreshing state on the chart …: expected 'absent' to be 'present'`
  - `the re-query tore the chart down to the loading placeholder: expected 'Loading Gantt chart...' to be 'no placeholder'`
  - `(a) after the answer: not the GanttView that painted the first rows: expected '2' to be '1'`
  - zh: `expected undefined to be '刷新中…'`

  The (d) control, the re-query-carries-the-query case and the failure case are green on base, as expected.
- **Head** `c1041d311`: all 11 cases green across both files (Leg 5).

## Reverse run and mutations

All from the committed head `c1041d311`. The two test files run with `--reporter=verbose`. Every leg restores from HEAD under a trap: blob `cdd9bca99` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Legs 2 to 4 went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor count (1 → 0) and that the blob moved before the run.

| Leg | Mutation | Predicted red | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Whole fix reverted to base (12 files), tests kept. On disk: `loadedOnceRef` 0, `RefreshIndicator` 0 | 3 change kinds + zh + the 7231 post-paint twin | `Tests 5 failed \| 6 passed (11)`, exactly those five |
| 2 | 7231 `finally` guard removed (`if (true …)`) | 7231 cases 1, 1b, 3 | `3 failed \| 8 passed`, exactly those three |
| 3 | Guard narrowed to its own mode | 7231 case 3 only | `1 failed \| 10 passed` |
| 4 | Re-query made silent | The failure pin only | `1 failed \| 10 passed` |
| 5 | None | none | `11 passed (11)` |

## Gates (at `c1041d311`)

Derived by hand from objectui's `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`, because `dispatch-gates.mjs` answers only for objectstack.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/ packages/i18n/`: `Test Files 147 passed (147)`, `Tests 1762 passed (1762)`, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-gantt^...' --concurrency=2`: 12/12 tasks.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt --filter @object-ui/i18n run type-check`: exit 0. Both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json` ran, and the latter includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
- `run lint` on both packages: exit 0, 0 errors. Warnings are the existing ones (plugin-gantt 436, i18n 33). None sits on a line this diff added in `ObjectGantt.tsx`, and none is in a locale pack.
- Exit 0, each:
  - changesets: `check-changeset-presence`, `-no-major`, `-overwrite`, `-fixed`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - text: `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`;
  - i18n: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:i18n-dead-keys` (the new key is not reported);
  - sources: `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:side-effects-array`;
  - tests: `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`.
- `check-eager-locale-catalogues`: NOT MEASURED. It answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET because `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` needs a console production build, so it is left to the performance-budget workflow.
- `check:changeset-claims` named three pending paragraphs that mention a touched file (6475, 6661, 6939). I re-read each: they cover `getGanttConfig`'s key set, `console.nav` strings, and the record-source order. None is falsified.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the bar shows.** It shows on every in-place re-read, not only on a changed query: the toolbar refresh, the write-readbacks and the invalidation reload. It reads the one `refreshing` flag the toolbar button already read. The changeset says so.
- **Changing the bound object.** A change to the bound source on a painted chart also refreshes in place. No shipped host does that without remounting by key (census 5744524200), and the object-schema gate window before such a re-query shows no bar, as on base.
- **Docs.** No README or docs page describes the gantt's loading or refresh behaviour, so none went false. The objectui#10035 change to the same seam added none either, so docs stayed off this file surface.
- **Out of scope, class (a).** Once any load fails, `error` is never cleared by a later successful reload, so the chart stays on the error screen. Measured at head with a throwaway probe (deleted, never committed): a failed first load, then a sort change. The second `find` ran with `$orderby {start_date: desc}` and succeeded, and the reading was `errorShown: true, chartMounted: false, recoveredRowShown: false`. The first load is non-silent in both trees, so base behaves the same and this diff does not move it. Handed to the seat to file.
